# netbox_virtual_machines (Data Source)

Lists virtual_machine objects matching the given filters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "netbox_virtual_machines" "test" {
  filters = [
    { name = "name", value = "test-virtual_machine" },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `filters` (Attributes Set) Query filters, sent as API list parameters. Supported names: cluster_group, cluster_group__n, cluster_id, cluster_id__n, device, device_id, device_id__n, id, id__empty, id__gt, id__gte, id__lt, id__lte, id__n, name, name__empty, name__ic, name__ie, name__iew, name__iregex, name__isw, name__n, name__nic, name__nie, name__niew, name__nisw, name__regex, owner_id, owner_id__n, platform, platform__n, platform_id, platform_id__n, region, region__n, role, role__n, role_id, role_id__n, site, site__n, site_id, site_id__n, status, status__empty, status__ic, status__ie, status__iew, status__iregex, status__isw, status__n, status__nic, status__nie, status__niew, status__nisw, status__regex, tag, tag__any, tag__n, tenant_id, tenant_id__n. Repeating a name sends that parameter once per value. Custom fields filter as cf_<field name>, e.g. cf_tier, with the field's own filter logic: loose is a case-insensitive substring match, exact an exact match. NetBox ignores names it has no custom field for, and such an entry does not narrow the result. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))
- `limit` (Number) The maximum number of objects to return from the API lookup. Defaults to 1000.
- `name_regex` (String) Go regular expression the name must match. Applied after the API query, which then fetches every object matching the filters; limit applies to the matches.

### Read-Only

- `virtual_machines` (Attributes List) The matching virtual_machines. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--virtual_machines))

<a id="nestedatt--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the query filter (the API list parameter).
- `value` (String) Value to filter by.


<a id="nestedatt--virtual_machines"></a>
### Nested Schema for `virtual_machines`

Read-Only:

- `cluster_id` (Number) Id of the cluster (a virtual machine needs a cluster or a site).
- `comments` (String)
- `config_template_id` (Number) Id of the config template.
- `created` (String)
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values by field name. Every value is a string; NetBox coerces numbers and booleans. A key removed from the map is cleared in NetBox (set {} to clear all).
- `description` (String)
- `device_id` (Number) Id of the device hosting the VM.
- `disk_size_mb` (Number) Disk size in MB. Once the machine has virtual disks NetBox computes it as their sum and it can no longer be set; leave it unset then.
- `id` (Number) NetBox id.
- `interface_count` (Number) Number of interfaces on the virtual machine.
- `last_updated` (String)
- `local_context_data` (String) Local config context data as JSON text (use jsonencode()).
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory in MB.
- `name` (String)
- `owner_id` (Number) Id of the owner the object is assigned to.
- `platform_id` (Number) Id of the platform.
- `primary_ip4_id` (Number) Id of the primary IPv4 address (managed by netbox_primary_ip).
- `primary_ip6_id` (Number) Id of the primary IPv6 address (managed by netbox_primary_ip).
- `role_id` (Number) Id of the functional device role.
- `serial` (String) Serial number.
- `site_id` (Number) Id of the site (a virtual machine needs a cluster or a site).
- `start_on_boot` (String) Power state the virtual machine takes when its host boots. One of: on, off, laststate.
- `status` (String) Operational status. One of: offline, active, planned, staged, failed, decommissioning, paused.
- `tags` (Set of String) Slugs of the tags assigned to the object (the provider's default_tags are added on top, see tags_all).
- `tags_all` (Set of String) Slugs of all tags on the object, including the provider's default_tags.
- `tenant_id` (Number) Id of the tenant.
- `url` (String)
- `vcpus` (Number) Number of virtual CPUs (fractions allowed).
- `virtual_disk_count` (Number) Number of virtual disks on the virtual machine.
- `virtual_machine_type_id` (Number) Id of the virtual machine type.
